sections.h2: What notice does a Missouri landlord have to give before an eviction?
sections.html:
It depends on why the landlord wants the tenant out. A landlord who is owed rent can skip the termination notice and go straight to court after demanding payment, while a landlord ending a tenancy with no rent default must give a written notice that runs one month. Missouri sets these two tracks in RSMo 535.020 and RSMo 441.060.

For a seller with a rented house, this split decides the schedule. If the tenant is behind, the clock starts with a rent demand and a filing. If the tenant is current and simply has to leave before closing, the clock starts with a written notice.

sections.h2: Is a rent demand required before a nonpayment case starts?
sections.html:
Yes. Under RSMo 535.020 the rent must have come due, the landlord or the landlord's agent must have demanded it from the tenant or whoever occupies the home, and it must remain unpaid. The landlord then signs an affidavit for an associate circuit judge that lists the rental terms, the amount actually due, the demand, and a description of the property.

The same section says the landlord does not have to give the one-month notice from section 441.060 first. That is why the summons in a nonpayment case carries a court date no more than twenty-one business days out (RSMo 535.030), while a lease-ending notice by itself takes a full month. RSMo 535.010 is the short rule behind it: when rent is not paid as agreed, the landlord may dispossess the tenant and any subtenants, using the procedure in chapter 535.

A landlord may add other unpaid sums from the lease to the same case, but the statute says those sums are not rent and a judgment for them alone does not entitle the landlord to possession.

sections.h2: How much written notice ends a month-to-month or at-will tenancy?
sections.html:
One month, in writing. RSMo 441.060 lets the person entitled to possession end a tenancy at will, a tenancy by sufferance, or any tenancy for less than one year by giving one month's written notice that tells the occupant to vacate.

An oral rental is treated as month to month under the same section. Either side may end it with one month's written notice. For a month-to-month tenancy the notice must say the tenancy ends on a rent-paying date at least one month after the other party receives it, so a notice handed over on the 20th for a tenancy that renews on the 1st cannot end the tenancy on the 1st that follows.

Tenants on a leased lot who own the mobile home sitting on it get a longer period. The landlord must give written notice that the tenancy ends not sooner than sixty days from the date the next rent payment comes due, even if the lease says something shorter.

sections.h2: What other notices can start or end a Missouri tenancy?
sections.html:
Three more notices come up often when a house is being sold with someone living in it. Each has its own statute and its own count of days.

  • Foreclosure occupant notice. After a trustee's sale, the new owner must tell a former residential tenant that the sale happened and that the occupant has at least ten business days to leave. No possession action may start inside that window (RSMo 534.030).
  • Abandonment notice. If rent has gone unpaid for thirty days and the landlord reasonably believes the tenant left for good, the landlord may post a notice on the door and mail it by first class and certified mail. The tenant has ten days to answer in writing before the landlord may treat the home as abandoned (RSMo 441.065).
  • Domestic violence protection. A tenant who is a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking cannot be evicted for that reason, and the statute gives an affirmative defense to rent owed after the tenant moves out when the landlord was told and any requested documents were supplied (RSMo 441.920).

sections.h2: Can a landlord skip court and remove a tenant?
sections.html:
No. RSMo 441.233 says a landlord or agent who removes or excludes a tenant or the tenant's belongings without judicial process and a court order, or who takes off doors or locks, is guilty of forcible entry and detainer under chapter 534. The same section covers willfully cutting electric, gas, water or sewer service, unless the landlord acts for health or safety reasons.

The one carve-out is the abandonment procedure in section 441.065. Outside that, a notice has to be followed by a judgment and an officer's writ before anyone is physically removed. A seller who owns a rented house should plan around that sequence instead of promising a buyer an empty house on a fixed date.

sections.h2: What does a notice mean for selling a rented Missouri house?
sections.html:
A notice sets the earliest realistic date the house can be vacant, and a nonpayment filing sets a faster but less predictable one. A sale of an occupied house is allowed, so the choice is between waiting out the notice and selling with the tenant in place.

  • Read the lease first. A written lease for a year or more is not ended by the one-month notice that applies to shorter tenancies.
  • Ask the buyer in writing whether it will take the home with the tenant in it, and put the answer in the contract.
  • Keep copies of every notice, mailing receipt and posting, because the court will want proof of what was given and when.
  • Count business days and rent-paying dates, not calendar guesses, before setting a closing date.

Ask the circuit clerk in the county where the house sits which forms the local court expects for a rent and possession filing.

faqs.q: How many days notice does a Missouri landlord have to give to evict for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: No set number of days applies to a rent case. After the landlord demands the rent and it stays unpaid, a verified statement can be filed with an associate circuit judge, and RSMo 535.020 says the one-month notice from section 441.060 is not required first.

faqs.q: Is one month's notice enough to end a month-to-month tenancy in Missouri?
faqs.a: Yes, if it is written and ends the tenancy on a rent-paying date at least one month after the other side receives it. The rule is in RSMo 441.060. A notice that lands in the middle of a rental period usually pushes the end date to the next rent date.

faqs.q: What notice does a tenant get when the house is foreclosed on?
faqs.a: At least ten business days. The new owner must send the occupant a notice by certified or registered mail when the name is known, or regular mail addressed to Occupant when it is not, and post a copy on the door, as RSMo 534.030 requires. The notice does not create a tenancy.

faqs.q: Can a landlord throw a tenant's belongings out after a notice expires?
faqs.a: Not on the strength of a notice alone. Belongings left after a court-ordered execution fall under RSMo 535.040, and items clearly labeled as a third party's property must be offered back by certified mail with five business days to recover them. Belongings left in a home that qualifies as abandoned follow RSMo 441.065.

faqs.q: Does a tenant who is a victim of domestic violence have special protection from eviction?
faqs.a: Yes. RSMo 441.920 bars eviction or a lease violation finding based on the tenant being, or being in imminent danger of becoming, a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking, with exceptions when the tenant let the named person in or the landlord reasonably believes that person threatens other occupants or the property.
